title: Aphids and the mosaic diseases they transmit to cowpeas

Header: Aphids and the mosaic diseases they transmit to cowpeas
e.g. Aphis craccivora (cowpea aphid), vector of mosaic diseases such as Cowpea aphid-borne mosaic potyvirus (CAMV)

Prevention: Use clean seed from disease-free plants
Avoid using shrivelled seeds with wrinkles
Use the correct planting density: 50 x 20 cm (erect variety); 50 x 30 cm (spreading variety); 100 x 100 cm (local:
Remove alternative aphid host plants from around the field (Weeds are generally host plants)
Plant during the early rains, especially if using the local
Plant a trap crop around the field to trap aphids which spread the disease
Monitoring: Regularly visit farm to look for signs of aphid infestation:
Presence of aphid colonies on the underside of leaves and stems
Presence of ants at apical part of plants
Presence of honeydew on leaves, pendules and stems
Look for signs of cowpea mosaic virus infection:
Leaf yellowing and deformation (folding at margin)
Restrictions: Apply early in the morning or late evening and use protective gear while spraying.
